name: Claude Squad

surfaces.label: the Claude Squad manager TUI: a single Go binary (Bubble Tea), installed as `cs` (README, install.sh default) or `claude-squad` (Homebrew formula, release archive). install.sh --name can pick any other name, which this row cannot see. It is a manager, not an agent: it does not run the agents itself. For every instance it runs `tmux new-session -d -s claudesquad_<title> -c <worktree> <program>`, so the agent (claude, codex, aider, gemini, amp ...) is a child of the tmux SERVER, not of `cs`, and a `cs` process has no agent among its children. Its own direct children are per instance: one long-lived `tmux attach-session -t claudesquad_<title>` on a pty, plus short-lived `tmux capture-pane` and `git diff` calls every 500 ms per active instance (`git diff --numstat` for unselected ones, full `git diff` for the selected one), and `capture-pane` every 100 ms for the selected instance's preview. Those children are always present, so a child signal cannot separate working from idle. The agent process is matched by its own row (claude-code, codex ...), and belongs to a squad when its cwd is under ~/.claude-squad/worktrees/ or its tmux session is named claudesquad_*. Subcommands `debug`, `version`, `reset`, `help`, `completion` and the help flags are short-lived and excluded by whole-token match. `cs` is also the name of the Coursier (Scala) launcher, so a bare `cs` match needs a second check: ~/.claude-squad/ exists. The registry schema cannot express that check, so the probe reports a Coursier `cs` as a Claude Squad TUI.

auto-yes daemon: `cs --daemon`, a hidden flag. Launched with setsid by the TUI on exit when auto_yes is on (config or -y/--autoyes). argv[0] is os.Executable(), so usually a full path. Polls every daemon_poll_interval ms (default 1000), and presses Enter in any session whose pane shows a permission prompt. Killed by the next TUI start via ~/.claude-squad/daemon.pid. It is not a session and has no turn.

working_signals.meaning: WEAK and unmeasured. The `cs` tree covers only the manager: its 500 ms poll (capture-pane, sha256 of the pane, git diff) and the redraw when a pane changes. The agents are under the tmux server, outside this tree. Use it only to say the manager is busy. For a squad session's turn, apply the agent's own row to the pane process: for Claude Code, a direct `caffeinate` child of the `claude` process. The manager also redraws a spinner and polls the selected pane every 100 ms, so an idle `cs` with several instances may sit above this floor and read as permanently working (inferred from app/app.go previewTickMsg and spinner.Tick, not measured).

waiting_signals.meaning: Claude Squad has no hooks and no status file for waiting. Where the pane program is Claude Code, the user's own ~/.claude/settings.json Notification hook fires inside the squad session exactly as it does outside one.

How Claude Squad itself decides: capture-pane text contains 'No, and tell Claude what to do differently' (claude), '(Y)es/(N)o/(D)on't ask again' (aider, program starts with aider) or 'Yes, allow once' (gemini, program starts with gemini). Only auto-yes acts on it, there is no status for it and no marker in state.json. For claude the test is program == 'claude' exactly, so it is off when default_program is an absolute path, which is what a default install writes (it is on for a bare `claude` from config or `cs -p claude`). Reads conversation text; not recommended for a monitor.

hooks.config: none: no hook, plugin or event mechanism in the source. Agent hooks configured in the agent itself still run inside squad sessions.

telemetry.how: none: no OpenTelemetry dependency in go.mod and no telemetry code in the source. The only log is $TMPDIR/claudesquad.log (os.TempDir), which is a debug log. The agents inside sessions export their own telemetry, if configured.

sources.claim: status Running/Ready is only 'pane text changed since the last 500 ms tick'; there is no turn signal. Changed => Running; unchanged and no prompt detected => Ready; unchanged and a prompt detected (only when the program string matches: claude exactly, aider*, gemini*) => status is left as it was (no set to Ready) and Enter is tapped if auto-yes. For any other program an unchanged pane is Ready even while a permission prompt is showing

notes: Claude Squad is a manager. It has no turn concept: its Running/Ready is a 500 ms pane-diff. To tell whether a squad session is working, find the agent process (a child of the tmux server) and use that agent's own row. The per-instance `tmux attach-session` children are never reported because no row in registry/agents/ matches a process named `tmux` (grep of the rows). If `cs` is not running the sessions still run: tmux keeps the agents alive, and state.json is a stale snapshot. Nothing here was run. Not verified: the pane process is `claude` itself or `$SHELL -c claude`, idle and busy CPU of `cs`, and how a Coursier `cs` looks in ps (that `cs` is Coursier's name is documented, its process shape was not observed). Matching caveats: (1) exclude_args are whole argv tokens after splitting ps output on spaces, so `cs -p "aider --help"` or `cs -p "codex debug"` would be dropped as if it were a short-lived subcommand; rare, accepted. (2) A Coursier `cs` is reported as Claude Squad until a second check exists; the schema has no way to require ~/.claude-squad/. (3) The daemon surface shares the row-level working_signals, which do not apply to it. Re-verified 2026-09-29 against the clone at ce1ffb4.
